reviewer.impersonation_disclaimer: Not a human reviewer. Issued under the owner governance amendment with requires_release_gate_amendment=true.
reviewer.method: read-only audit. No model call was made, no artifact was sealed or modified, no calibration round was started.

diff_recomputation.method: recomputed changed_fields and the changed flag from human_label against the frozen draft_label, without trusting the export's own values

frame_fitness_assessment.purpose: Verify before sealing that both pre-registered gates can actually bind on this frame, rather than being satisfiable trivially.

predicted_negative_stratum.why: the negative stratum is not empty of true positives, so tightening the positive decision will push this metric upward and the gate has real force

frame_fitness_assessment.verdict: The frame is fit for purpose. Neither gate is trivially satisfied and neither is unreachable by construction.

diagnosis_independently_reconfirmed.statement: Baseline precision on this fresh, independent development frame is 0.533, against 0.525 measured on the now-spent heldout40. The over-prediction diagnosis is reproduced on a sample the model was never evaluated against, so it is a systematic property of the extractor rather than an artefact of the earlier 40-item draw.
diagnosis_independently_reconfirmed.significance: This retires any hypothesis that the heldout result was sampling noise.

narrow_corridor_warning.statement: The false-omission headroom is thin. The negative stratum currently sits at 2 of 15 and the gate permits at most 3 of 15. Calibration must raise precision from 0.533 to 0.80 while adding at most one additional miss in that stratum.
narrow_corridor_warning.implication: Naive tightening of the materiality rubric will very likely trade precision gains for omissions and fail the second gate. The work needs to sharpen the boundary rather than simply move it.
narrow_corridor_warning.not_a_reason_to_change_the_gate: The 0.20 bound was set a priori in the pre-registration before any measurement. Relaxing it now, having seen the baseline, would be exactly the goalpost movement the owner's option A decision was meant to avoid.

statistical_fragility_disclosed.statement: A 15-item negative stratum makes the false-omission rate coarse: one item flipping moves it by 0.067, and the pass/fail boundary sits between 3 and 4 items. The development gate on this metric is therefore noisy and should be read as a coarse guard against regression, not as a precise estimate.
statistical_fragility_disclosed.handling: Recorded as a known limitation of the pre-registered design rather than corrected mid-round. The heldout frame's 20-item negative stratum is slightly better but shares the same character, and this limitation must be disclosed in any report that cites a false-omission rate.

adjudication_intensity_note.observation: The owner changed 9 of 45 items here against 25 of 40 on the earlier heldout. The direction of change is coherent rather than random: the draft carried 22 items at materiality at or above 2 and the adjudicated gold carries 18, so the changes tighten in the same direction as the known over-prediction.
adjudication_intensity_note.assessment: A lower change rate is consistent with a stronger drafter and with an owner more practised in the rubric. It is not by itself evidence of reduced scrutiny, and nothing in the record contradicts the adjudication. Flagged only so that a future reader comparing the two sessions is not surprised.

what_this_does_not_approve: any access to, materialization of, or sampling from the heldout frame
any change to the 0.80 precision gate or the 0.20 false-omission gate
any change to the retired heldout identities, the frozen designs, or the recorded failed rounds
marking P4.2a done or unlocking P4.2b or P4.3
